title: Juniper and the Locker
premise: Juniper Hartwell, seventeen and eldest of four, has spent two years holding his family together while his mother works hospital night shifts — and he's built his entire reputation at Carver High on never letting anyone see the cracks. When his history teacher pairs him with Theo Vance, his smug academic rival, for a semester-long capstone on local civic history, Juniper expects misery; instead they unearth a decades-old school board cover-up involving condemned housing that displaced Juniper's own family — and a payoff still funding the district. As Juniper's home life unravels toward eviction and Theo's school-board-president father closes ranks around them, the boys must choose between protecting their futures and exposing the truth. In the end, Juniper testifies at the final board meeting with his siblings in the audience, trading his scholarship prospects for accountability — and discovering that belonging was never something he had to earn alone.
about_author: Marguerite Eastwick is the pen name of a former social studies teacher who spent eleven years watching students carry more than any syllabus accounted for. She writes young adult fiction about kids who are competent beyond their years and tired beyond their age.

chapters.title: Fine Is a Full-Time Job
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV opens on a 5 a.m. routine: packing lunches, waking three siblings, covering for Mom's double shift, then performing effortless normalcy at school. A near-miss with a truancy officer establishes the stakes. Emotional beat: competence as armor, and the loneliness underneath it.

chapters.title: The Seating Chart Betrayal
chapters.summary: Mr. Okafor announces semester capstone pairs; Juniper is matched with Theo Vance, who once mocked his thrift-store shoes in front of everyone. They argue over topic selection until Okafor assigns one himself: 'Carver's Founding Families.' POV alternates briefly to Theo, revealing he resents being his father's trophy. Beat: reluctant collision.

chapters.title: Archive Hours
chapters.summary: Forced together in the county archive after school — hours Juniper can't afford because he watches his siblings — Juniper brings seven-year-old Wren along, and Theo unexpectedly entertains her. Among founding documents, Juniper spots a gap: a missing 1974 rezoning record. Beat: first crack in the rivalry.

chapters.title: What Grandma Buried
chapters.summary: Juniper asks his grandmother about the old neighborhood; she goes quiet, then hands him a shoebox of photographs of houses that no longer exist — including the address where his family lived before 'the move.' He realizes the displacement wasn't random. Beat: personal history becomes evidence.

chapters.title: Theo's Perfect House
chapters.summary: Juniper visits Theo's home to work and sees the other side of town: money, ease, and coldness. Theo's father, Board President Richard Vance, interrogates Juniper about his family with unsettling interest. Beat: envy curdles into understanding — both boys are surviving different prisons.

chapters.title: The Eviction Notice
chapters.summary: A rent hike notice arrives; Mom picks up more shifts and starts sleeping through her days off. Juniper hides the notice from his siblings and from school. Meanwhile Theo finds the 1974 minutes in a misfiled box: land sold below value to a development company. Beat: the past and present start converging.

chapters.title: Signatures and Shell Companies
chapters.summary: Research montage chapter: the development company traces back through shell entities to names still on the school board's donor wall — including a Vance. Juniper wants to go public immediately; Theo urges caution, terrified of his father. First real fight. Beat: loyalty vs. truth takes shape between them.

chapters.title: Wren's Question
chapters.summary: Little Wren asks why they can't live in one of the houses in Grandma's pictures. Juniper lies badly, then can't sleep. He drafts an email to a local journalist and deletes it. Beat: the weight of being the one who knows things small people shouldn't have to.

chapters.title: Midterms and Meltdowns
chapters.summary: Juniper fails a chemistry midterm for the first time ever; his scholarship counselor flags it. Theo covers for him with Okafor without being asked — an act of quiet loyalty that undoes Juniper more than kindness usually does. Beat: letting someone help is its own vulnerability.

chapters.title: The Retaliation
chapters.summary: After Theo requests sealed board records through a public-records act, his father discovers it. Theo arrives at school with a split lip and a story about a doorframe. He pulls away from Juniper, resuming the old armor. Beat: fear winning, alliance fracturing.

chapters.title: Grandma's Testimony
chapters.summary: Grandma finally tells the whole story: families were promised relocation assistance that never came, complaints buried by the same men now honored on plaques. She makes Juniper promise not to burn his future for the dead — but her hands shake as she says it. Beat: generational cost made explicit.

chapters.title: The Whistleblower
chapters.summary: A retired district secretary contacts them after word of their project spreads: she kept copies of everything, waiting thirty years for someone to ask. The file includes relocation fund ledgers showing money diverted into board discretionary accounts. Beat: hope arrives with teeth.

chapters.title: Okafor Knows
chapters.summary: Mr. Okafor confronts them gently — he recognized the rezoning gap weeks ago and chose to let them find it. He warns them what going public costs and offers an out: submit the safe version, graduate clean. Both boys say no, separately, without consulting each other. Beat: conviction crystallizing.

chapters.title: Mom Comes Home Early
chapters.summary: Mom loses her job when the hospital cuts night staff; she comes home at dawn and finds the eviction notice Juniper hid, plus the research spread across the kitchen table. Instead of anger: exhaustion, then a fierce, quiet 'Do it.' Beat: the secret-keeper is finally seen.

chapters.title: Leak
chapters.summary: They give the file to journalist Dana Okonkwo, who warns them publication will trigger a firestorm before graduation. Within days, anonymous threats arrive; Juniper's locker is vandalized — 'JUNIPER AND THE LOCKER' scrawled as a taunt about what else might be inside. Beat: exposure begins, danger follows.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Richard Vance summons Juniper privately: full ride to state school, rent covered, records quietly returned, in exchange for recanting. It would solve every problem Juniper has. He walks out without answering — and throws up in the parking lot. Beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Broken Trust
chapters.summary: Juniper, desperate after another eviction warning, almost accepts. Theo finds out and feels betrayed; Juniper accuses Theo of having the luxury of principles. Their worst fight yet ends the partnership — and Okafor dissolves the capstone pair. Beat: rock bottom, alone.

chapters.title: What Wren Packed
chapters.summary: Packing boxes with his siblings, Juniper finds Wren has hidden her favorite toys in his backpack 'so you'll have them wherever you go.' He realizes they've been watching him sacrifice all along. He calls Theo. No speech — just 'I'm sorry. Help me finish it.' Beat: humility and repair.

chapters.title: The Board Meeting
chapters.summary: Climax. At the packed final board meeting, Juniper testifies with the ledgers, Grandma beside him, siblings in the front row. Theo stands up against his father publicly. The room fractures; a state oversight official in attendance requests the records. Beat: truth spoken at maximum personal cost.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Vance resigns under investigation; the article wins attention, though nothing changes overnight. Juniper loses the guaranteed scholarship but gains an unexpected aid package funded by alumni ashamed of the cover-up — imperfect justice, honestly priced. Beat: consequences without fairy-tale neatness.

chapters.title: Capstone
chapters.summary: Juniper and Theo present their project one last time — not the safe version, the true one — to applause and some stony silence. Okafor gives them top marks and a warning: 'Truth-telling is a habit. Start young.' Beat: earned recognition, identity transformed.

chapters.title: Juniper and the Open Door
chapters.summary: Resolution. Moving day into a modest repaired unit in the redeveloped district — part of the restitution settlement. Wren unpacks her toys from his backpack herself. Juniper, exhausted and lighter, lets Theo's family drive them. Final line echoes the opening: everything is fine — and this time, it actually is. Beat: belonging, unearned and given.
